Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

openfhe.R 1.6.1

  • The vendored library is OpenFHE 1.6.1. Every class, method and enum that the Python package openfhe 1.6.1.0 exposes has an R counterpart. Its tests and examples are run as tests of this package, except one example that needs a 128-bit build of the library.

  • Contexts, keys and ciphertexts saved by openfhe.R 1.5.1.2, in the binary or the JSON format, are read by this version.

  • BinFHEParamSet has the 112 members of OpenFHE 1.6.1. Every member except TOY and MEDIUM has a new integer value, so code must refer to members by name (BinFHEParamSet$STD128), never by number.

  • OpenFHE 1.6.1 redefines the predefined Binary FHE parameter sets under their old names. BinFHEParamSet$STD128_AP now works only with BinFHEMethod$AP.

  • bin_fhe_context() builds the context for arbitrary-function evaluation whenever arb_func, log_q, n or time_optimization is supplied, as the C++ library does. Before, supplying arb_func = FALSE alone built the Boolean-gate context, which has different parameters.

  • serialize_eval_keys() to a file that cannot be opened is an error. Before, the JSON format returned TRUE and wrote nothing.

  • find_automorphism_index() and find_automorphism_indices() refuse a value outside the 32-bit integer range.

  • length() of the object share_keys() returns is the number of shares.

  • Functions that return an encrypted value, a key or another handle no longer go through the ‘S7’ constructor, which saves about 45 microseconds per call.

  • bin_bt_key_gen() gains the argument internal32.

  • The help pages for bin_fhe_context(), bin_bt_key_gen() and bin_clear_bt_keys() have a section on memory. The bootstrapping keys of a context can occupy several gigabytes that R’s garbage collector does not see; bin_clear_bt_keys() releases them at once.

  • bin_encrypt() defaults to output = BinFHEOutput$BOOTSTRAPPED, and get_bootstrap_depth() to SecretKeyDist$UNIFORM_TERNARY, as in OpenFHE 1.6.1.

  • eval_add(), eval_sub() and eval_mult(), with their _in_place and _mutable forms, accept every operand order and type the C++ library declares: a plaintext or a number as the first operand, and complex numbers for a CKKS context with complex data. eval_sub(2, ct) now calls the library’s own scalar-first subtraction.

  • eval_poly(), eval_chebyshev() and their _linear and _ps forms accept integer and complex coefficient vectors as well as doubles. An integer vector is now evaluated with integer arithmetic; it was converted to double before. At OpenFHE 1.6.1 the Paterson-Stockmeyer Chebyshev evaluator returns wrong values for integer coefficients, so pass whole-number Chebyshev coefficients as doubles.

  • eval_bin_gate() gains extended. eval_floor() and compress() take the library defaults roundbits = 0 and towers_left = 1. level_reduce() and level_reduce_in_place() accept NULL for the evaluation key. get_bootstrap_depth() gains approx_mod_depth. multiparty_key_gen() accepts a list of secret keys. get_length() works on an LWECiphertext.

  • New set_* functions change one parameter of a BFVParams, BGVParams or CKKSParams object after it has been constructed (set_multiplicative_depth(), set_ring_dim() and 30 others; see ?ccparams_setters), so a parameter object can be built step by step as the OpenFHE examples do. format() and print() of a parameter object show every field.

  • New gen_crypto_context() builds a context from a parameter object and enables no feature, as OpenFHE’s GenCryptoContext() does. fhe_context() is unchanged.

  • make_ckks_packed_plaintext() accepts params with complex values.

  • New evaluation functions: eval_add_many(), eval_add_many_in_place(), eval_mult_many(), eval_merge(), eval_linear_wsum(), eval_linear_wsum_mutable(), eval_inner_product(), eval_sum_rows(), eval_sum_cols() with eval_sum_rows_key_gen() and eval_sum_cols_key_gen(), eval_at_index(), composed_eval_mult() and eval_mult_keys_gen().

  • New in-place forms eval_square_in_place(), rescale_in_place(), relinearize_in_place(), eval_add_mutable_in_place(), eval_sub_mutable_in_place() and eval_mult_mutable_in_place(), and the unchecked forms eval_add_in_place_no_check(), eval_mult_no_check() and eval_mult_no_relin_no_check().

  • Proxy re-encryption: re_key_gen() and re_encrypt().

  • make_string_plaintext() encodes a character string.

  • New accessors. On a context: get_modulus(), get_modulus_ckks(), get_root_of_unity(), get_scheme(), set_scheme_id(), serialized_object_name(), serialized_version(), clear_all_ckks_caches(), clear_bootstrap_precom(), clear_scheme_switch_precom(), get_plaintext_for_decrypt(), the automorphism key index queries get_existing_eval_automorphism_key_indices(), get_eval_automorphism_no_key_indices() and get_unique_values(), and set_multiplicative_depth(), set_eval_add_count(), set_key_switch_count(), set_pre_num_hops() and set_noise_estimate() on a live context. On a ciphertext: clone(), clone_empty(), number_ciphertext_elements(), get_elements(), set_elements(), remove_element(), get_hop_level(), set_hop_level() and set_encoding_type(). On a plaintext: encode(), decode(), get_element_modulus(), get_encoding_params() and set_format().

  • get_modulus(), ring_dimension() and get_cyclotomic_order() work on an ElementParams object; get_batch_size(), get_plaintext_modulus() and the new get_plaintext_generator() on an EncodingParams object; get_key_tag() and set_key_tag() on an EvalKey; get_crypto_context() on a public or secret key.

  • New classes DCRTPoly and SchemeBase (opaque handles) and enum Format.

  • Key switching: key_switch_gen(), key_switch(), key_switch_in_place(), key_switch_ext() and key_switch_down_first_element(). multi_mult_eval_key() completes the threshold multiplication-key protocol. sparse_key_gen() is bound as the C++ library declares it.

  • clear_eval_sum_keys(), get_all_contexts(), and enable_precompute_crt_tables_after_deserializaton() with its disable_ counterpart.

  • eval_chebyshev_function_ptxt() evaluates a Chebyshev approximation in the clear, and get_multiplicative_depth_by_coeff_vector() gives the depth a polynomial evaluation consumes.

  • eval_powers() and eval_cheby_polys() compute the powers, or the Chebyshev polynomials, of a ciphertext once, as an object of the new class SeriesPowers; eval_poly_with_precomp() and eval_chebyshev_series_with_precomp() then evaluate any number of series of the same degree from it.

  • eval_bootstrap_precompute() computes the plaintexts of CKKS bootstrapping after a setup with precompute = FALSE, and eval_bootstrap_stc_first() runs the slots-encoding variant of bootstrapping.

  • CKKS functional bootstrapping, which refreshes a ciphertext and applies a function to it in one step. For a look-up table on integers: eval_fbt_setup(), eval_fbt(), eval_fbt_no_decoding() and eval_hom_decoding(); for several tables on one input, eval_mvb_precompute(), eval_mvb() and eval_mvb_no_decoding(); with get_hermite_trig_coefficients(), get_fbt_depth() and eval_hermite_trig_series(). For a Fourier series on real values: eval_fe_func_bootstrap_setup(), eval_fe_func_bootstrap(), eval_fe_func_bootstrap_precompute(), eval_fe_func_bootstrap_with_precomp() and get_fefbt_depth().

  • The RLWE schemelet that functional bootstrapping takes its input from: schemelet_get_element_params(), schemelet_encrypt_coeff(), schemelet_decrypt_coeff(), schemelet_mod_switch(), schemelet_convert_rlwe_to_ckks(), schemelet_convert_ckks_to_rlwe() and schemelet_get_q_prime(), with the new class PolyVector (length(), clone(), -, switch_modulus()).

  • Scheme switching between CKKS and FHEW. From CKKS to FHEW: eval_ckks_to_fhew_setup(), eval_ckks_to_fhew_key_gen(), eval_ckks_to_fhew_precompute() and eval_ckks_to_fhew(). From FHEW to CKKS: eval_fhew_to_ckks_setup(), eval_fhew_to_ckks_key_gen() and eval_fhew_to_ckks(). Both ways: eval_scheme_switching_setup(), eval_scheme_switching_key_gen(), eval_compare_switch_precompute(), eval_compare_scheme_switching(), eval_min_scheme_switching(), eval_max_scheme_switching() and their _alt forms. The parameters are an object of the new class SchSwchParams, with a set_ and a get_ function per field (see ?SchSwchParams). Also get_bin_cc_for_scheme_switch(), set_bin_cc_for_scheme_switch(), get_swk_fc(), set_swk_fc() and set_params_from_ckks_cryptocontext().

  • New classes SchemeSwitchingDataSerializer and SchemeSwitchingDataDeserializer write and read everything a scheme-switching computation needs in another session, with set_data_directory(), serialize_scheme_switching_data(), deserialize_scheme_switching_data() and get_raw_ciphertext(). Unlike the C++ classes they have no default directory.

  • Binary FHE, public-key encryption: bin_key_gen_pair(), bin_pub_key_gen(), bin_key_gen_n(), bin_key_switch_gen() and switch_ct_to_qn(), with the new classes LWEPublicKey, LWEKeyPair and LWESwitchingKey. bin_encrypt() accepts an LWEPublicKey in place of the secret key.

  • Binary FHE, bootstrapping keys as objects: get_bt_key(), get_bt_key_map(), bin_bt_key_load(), bin_bt_key_map_load_single_element(), bin_clear_bt_keys(), get_switch_key(), get_public_key(), has_internal32_refresh_key() and has_internal32_switch_key(), with the new class RingGSWBTKey.

  • fhe_serialize() and fhe_deserialize() handle the Binary FHE classes BinFHEContext, LWECiphertext, LWEPrivateKey, LWEPublicKey and RingGSWBTKey, so a Boolean circuit can be set up in one session and evaluated in another.

  • Binary FHE, other additions: bin_bootstrap(), eval_constant(), eval_decomp(); the parameter accessors get_n(), get_big_n(), get_q(), get_big_q() and get_beta(); get_pt_modulus(), set_modulus() and set_pt_modulus() on an LWECiphertext; get_modulus() and get_length() on LWE ciphertexts and keys, which also compare with == and !=; serialized_object_name() and serialized_version() on a BinFHEContext.

  • Serialization in memory. fhe_serialize() with no file name returns the serialized object, a raw vector for the binary format and a character string for JSON, and the new fhe_deserialize_string() reads it back. serialize_eval_keys() with no file name does the same for the key registries, with the new deserialize_eval_keys_string().

  • fhe_serialize() and fhe_deserialize() handle EvalKey and EvalKeyMap objects, and fhe_serialize() a list of EvalKey objects (in memory).

  • serialize_eval_keys() gains cc, to serialize the keys of one context.

  • New serialize_eval_bootstrap_key() and deserialize_eval_bootstrap_key() write and read the automorphism keys that CKKS bootstrapping uses.

  • Integers that can exceed 53 bits are exchanged as strings of decimal digits, because an R number cannot hold them exactly. get_scaling_factor_int() now returns such a string, and set_scaling_factor_int() accepts one. Arguments of this kind also accept a whole number of at most 2^53.

  • The plaintext_modulus argument of BFVParams() and BGVParams() accepts any 64-bit value; values above 2^31 were previously turned into NA. get_plaintext_modulus() returns a string of decimal digits when the modulus is above 2^53.

openfhe.R 1.5.1.2

CRAN release: 2026-09-25

  • Under R CMD check the package caps OpenFHE at two threads.

  • set_num_threads() now sets the cap through OpenFHE’s own thread controls rather than the OpenMP runtime, and returns the cap in effect (invisibly).

  • The package now installs on musl-based Linux (Alpine).

  • rlang is declared in Imports.

  • Every handle the package passes between R and C++ now carries its type, and every binding checks that type before using the pointer.

  • bin_fhe_context() returns an object of the new BinFHEContext class instead of the base OpenFHEObject. The boolean-circuit context and the CryptoContext used by BFV, BGV, and CKKS are therefore distinct classes, and passing one where the other belongs is an error rather than a silent misuse.

  • OpenFHEObject, the base class, is now abstract. It was never useful to construct directly, and every handle now belongs to a concrete class.

  • decrypt() accepts its arguments in either order, matching the C++ library, which declares both. decrypt(private_key, ciphertext) is now equivalent to decrypt(ciphertext, private_key).

openfhe.R 1.5.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-08-23

  • Fixed undefined behavior in the vendored OpenFHE library reported by CRAN’s UBSAN check platforms. RingGSWAccumulator::SignedDigitDecompose sign-extended a balanced digit by shifting a signed value into and past the sign bit, which is undefined in C++17. The vendored library now carries the upstream fix (OpenFHE PR #1238), which computes the same digits without signed shifts. Results are unchanged.

  • The eval_sign() example in the BinFHE vignette and its corresponding test are skipped on CRAN, where their bootstrapping-key generation dominated the check time. Both still run on CI and locally.

openfhe.R 1.5.1

CRAN release: 2026-08-21

Initial release. An R interface to the OpenFHE C++ library for fully homomorphic encryption, with a binding surface that mirrors openfhe-python.

  • Supports the BFV, BGV, and CKKS schemes for computation on encrypted integers and approximate reals, plus BinFHE (FHEW/TFHE) for Boolean circuits over encrypted bits.

  • Provides threshold (multiparty) FHE, including interactive bootstrapping, for computations shared across several key-holders.

  • Built on S7 classes and cpp11 bindings; the OpenFHE C++ library is vendored and built from source, so the package version tracks the library version.

  • Ships an API tour vignette plus worked examples of CKKS bootstrapping and BinFHE Boolean circuits.
